directAnswer: To update a pull request, you need to push your changes to the branch associated with the pull request. The pull request will automatically reflect these changes.
summary: This guide explains how to update a pull request by pushing changes to the associated branch and addresses common questions.

sections.heading: Understanding Pull Requests
sections.body: A pull request (PR) is a request to merge code changes from one branch into another. Updating a PR involves making changes to the branch and pushing those changes.

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Steps
sections.body: The steps to update a pull request may vary slightly depending on the platform (e.g., GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket).

steps.title: Make Changes Locally
steps.detail: Edit your files in the local repository to implement the desired changes.

steps.title: Commit Your Changes
steps.detail: Run `git add .` to stage your changes, followed by `git commit -m 'Your message'` to commit them.

steps.title: Push Changes to Remote Branch
steps.detail: Execute `git push origin your-branch-name` to update the remote branch associated with the pull request.

steps.title: Check the Pull Request
steps.detail: Visit the pull request page on your platform to ensure the changes are reflected.

faqs.question: What if I need to change the base branch of my pull request?
faqs.answer: You can change the base branch by navigating to the pull request page and selecting a different base branch from the dropdown menu.

faqs.question: Can I update a pull request after it has been approved?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can update a pull request even after it has been approved. The approval will be removed until the changes are reviewed again.

faqs.question: How do I resolve merge conflicts in a pull request?
faqs.answer: You can resolve merge conflicts by pulling the latest changes from the base branch into your branch, resolving conflicts locally, and then pushing the resolved changes.

caveats: Ensure you are pushing to the correct branch associated with the pull request to avoid confusion.
If your pull request is already merged, you cannot update it; you will need to create a new pull request.
